The paper proposes a machine learning-based approach to reduce the electromagnetic signature of ferromagnetic vessels.
The method used is ridge regression, a type of machine learning algorithm.
The approach is efficient in terms of computational efforts, speed, and accuracy.
Over 90% reduction in signature is achieved using the proposed approach.
The approach is validated on a simulated model of a prototype submarine.
21 tri-axial DG coils are used in the simulation.
The relative permeability of the ferromagnetic tube is 200.
The thickness of the ferromagnetic tube is 0.1 mm.
The length of the ferromagnetic tube is 20 mm.
The outer radius of the ferromagnetic tube is 1.4 mm.
The reference current used to compute the individual coil effects is 3 A.
The magnetostatic solver of Opera-3D is used to predict the DG OFF magnetic signature.
Opera software is used to validate the proposed approach.
The longitudinal component is reduced by 84.78% when DG coils are placed inside the hull.
The longitudinal component is reduced by 75.17% when DG coils are placed outside the hull.
The arthwartship and vertical components are also significantly reduced.
The proposed approach handles multicollinearity issues and provides a stable solution.
The ridge regression approach is computationally efficient and fast.
